answer: A proof-of-agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to burn stake at a bonded wharf registry before trading on the river of agent-to-agent payments, where every interaction is attested and slashed. If one identity spawns a spiral of fakes, each fake must post fresh collateral and pay per-attestation verification costs, so faking identities becomes strictly more expensive than behaving — attackers bleed capital linearly while honest agents recover slash revenue.
